title: Microrehearsal Cadet Playbook (WIP)
content:
Purpose:
This is a working playbook for running small, repeatable "microrehearsals" that exercise cross-functional rollout paths: canaries, A/B splits, and emergency reversion.

Why a separate microrehearsal doc?
- Most canary runbooks focus on 'real' rollout time. We need short (15–45m) rehearsals that teams can run frequently to validate the choreography, tooling, and signals without impacting production customers.
- Emphasis on rehearsing the human/communication flows, synthetic traffic generation, and telemetry plumbing (alerts, dashboards, tracing).

Scope and constraints:
- Intended audience: release engineers, product owners, SRE oncall, program managers, solutions/SEs.
- Not for full production canaries or scale tests. Use dedicated rehearsal namespace and traffic tokens.
- All runs must be tagged in Jira and have a rollback drill scheduled.

Rehearsal types (quick reference):
1) Canary Switch Drill (15–25m)
   - Purpose: validate traffic split controls + immediate rollback path.
   - Traffic: 1% synthetic routed to candidate; 99% baseline traffic generator.
   - Key signals: 95th p90 latency delta, error spikes, cost per token anomaly.

2) Safety-Triggered Reversion (30–45m)
   - Purpose: simulate a signal that triggers automated fallback (e.g., hallucination metric or policy violation).
   - Traffic: targeted cohort (support-email like prompts) created by persona script.
   - Key signals: content-safety alert (QA classifier), quality regression on golden prompts.

3) Human-in-Loop Failover (20–40m)
   - Purpose: exercise comms and manual rollback (SRE -> product -> comms).
   - Traffic: low-volume but diverse synthetic set.
   - Key signals: manual escalation checklist, oncall handoff latencies.

4) A/B Data Integrity Check (30–40m)
   - Purpose: validate metric parity collection between control and variant (telemetry, attribution).
   - Traffic: balanced synthetic split (50/50) for a short window.

Pre-run checklist (10m ops prep):
- Create Jira task with tag "microrehearsal" and link to this doc.
- Reserve rehearsal namespace + tokens. Confirm no real-customer tokens are used.
- Notify stakeholders (SRE, product, SE, comms) on #rollouts-rehearsals channel 24h & 1h prior.
- Confirm dashboards listed below are up and show baseline.
- Sanity-run synthetic generator for 5m to ensure routing and attribution are correct.
- Confirm run duration and abort time in Jira.

Synthetic traffic recipe (example snippets, copy/paste friendly):
- generator config (pseudo-yaml):
  - name: support-cadet-1
  - rate: 20req/min
  - prompt_bank: support_triage_v2 (50 items)
  - metadata: {region: us-west, persona: "support-enduser"}
  - attribution: header X-Rehearsal-Id: RHL-<jira>

- Persona banks to seed:
  - support-agent: short prompts asking clarifying questions, multi-turn examples (20 variants)
  - search-refiner: long search queries + expected reranker output (15 variants)
  - short-chat: 1–3 token interactive queries to exercise prefix-caching

Observability checklist (must be validated before/after run):
- Dashboards: token-cost by model, route-level latency (p50/p90/p95), error-rate (4xx/5xx), model-confidence/QA-score metric.
- Traces: a sample of N=10 traces for the candidate route exported to tracing storage.
- Logs: ensure audit events (route-change, rollout-commit, traffic-slice-assignment) appear in the same minute as the action.
- Alerts: test synthetic alert: trigger an artificially elevated error for 1 minute and confirm alerting pipeline routes to #oncall and PagerDuty.

Metrics and thresholds (starter values — adjust per product):
- Latency p95: no >20% increase over baseline for >5m.
- Error rate (500s): no >0.5% absolute increase for >3m.
- Token cost delta: no >30% increase sustained for >10m.
- Golden prompt quality (BLEU-like or eval score): >3 point drop triggers review.
- Content safety classifier fail rate: >0.1% triggers automatic rollback.

Decision matrix (operator quickflow):
- If ANY safety classifier alert AND human review confirms -> immediate rollback to baseline and incident creation.
- If latency p95 > threshold AND error-rate below threshold -> throttle exposure to 0.1% and monitor for 5m; if still high -> rollback.
- If metric parity fails in A/B data -> pause experiment and open investigation ticket (tag: data-integrity).

Run roles & roster (example):
- Run Lead: coordinates the drill, hits the final rollback button. (Product / Release Eng)
- Traffic Operator: starts/stops synthetic generator, adjusts split. (Release Eng / SRE)
- Observability Lead: monitors dashboards, posts signals, collects traces. (SRE)
- Safety Reviewer: validates any content-safety alerts. (Trust & Safety or Applied ML)
- Communications: drafts customer-facing and internal status messages. (Comms/CS)
- Oncall backup: available to act if the primary doesn't respond.

Slack/Comms templates (fill-in):
- Pre-run: "FYI: microrehearsal RHL-<jira> starting at <time> in rehearsal-namespace. Lead: <name>. Expected duration: <mins>."
- Alert example: "ALERT: Rehearsal RHL-<jira> observed p95 latency spike to <value>ms (>threshold). Observability: <link>. Run Lead: <name>."
- Rollback notice: "ROLLBACK: Rehearsal RHL-<jira> rollback executed at <time> due to <reason>. Incident: <jira-incident>."

Post-run artifacts and checklist (15–30m):
- Save trends snapshot from dashboards (export PNGs).
- Collect sample traces + 5 flagged request IDs.
- Quick retro: 15m asynchronous notes in Jira comment: what worked / what broke / followups.
- Tag any instrumentation gaps as tickets (priority: P2 if telemetry missing for control/variant).

Templates for common followups (short descriptions):
- Instrumentation gap ticket: describe missing metric, where expected, minimal reproducible steps and owner.
- Data parity investigation: include SQL to sample attribution, time-bounded window, and expected event counts.

Playbook quick-fixes (for rehearsal scale):
- If synthetic generator attribution missing -> restart generator with explicit X-Rehearsal-Id header (often the root cause).
- If alert not firing -> confirm alert rule query timeframe and that rehearsal namespace is included.
- If rollback button fails due to auth -> have emergency CLI script ready with elevated token in vault.

Safety and compliance notes:
- Do not use PII in synthetic prompt banks. If you must, mask or use structured placeholders.
- Rehearsal tokens must be scoped to rehearsal namespace and audited.
- For private deployments demos, ensure customer data is never used in rehearsal scripts.

Open questions / discussion items (brainstorm):
- Should rehearsals have a weekly cadence and rotating owner? Pros: builds muscle. Cons: operational overhead.
- How to surface subtle quality regressions automatically beyond golden prompts? Consider sampling user-facing conversations and a lightweight human review panel.
- Can we build a self-serve 'rehearsal generator' in Console so non-ReleaseEng people can schedule microrehearsals?

TODOs (short list):
- [ ] Finalize minimal persona banks for support/search/chat (assigned: Miguel).
- [ ] Create a Console button prototype to start a rehearsal namespace (assigned: Jonah).
- [ ] Add rehearsal taxonomy to Confluence page (assigned: Aisha).

Notes to self / rough ideas (informal):
- Might be useful to have a "noise knob" to raise token variance to stress kernel selection path.
- Could pair this with Optimize recommendations: run microrehearsal then have Optimize suggest batching/quantization changes on the candidate model.

References and links:
- Confluence: https://confluence.internal/redwood/rollout-rehearsals (canonical)
- Jira tag: JIRA-INF-2345 (template for microrehearsal tasks)
- GitHub: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rollout-scripts (synthetic generator repo)

If you're reading this and want to run a microrehearsal: ping me (Aisha) on #rollouts-rehearsals and include a 30m window. We'll try a dry-run first.
